abort_accounting: Every repetition appears in the final report with repetition ID, exact terminal status, last completed phase, physical dollars spent, strategy dollars accrued, verified results earned, outstanding reservation state, and stop reason. Whole-study physical spend includes aborted repetitions. Positive scientific claims require ALL 3 matched repetitions completed; fewer: INCONCLUSIVE_INCOMPLETE_REPETITIONS. Aborted repetitions stay out of matched pooled treatment-effect math but in the whole-study expenditure/abort ledger.
accounting_rule: Two ledgers: (1) PHYSICAL STUDY LEDGER — actual dollars physically paid; the common first acquisition is physically paid once. (2) STANDALONE STRATEGY LEDGERS — B is charged FULL first-acquisition cost; C is charged FULL first-acquisition cost PLUS full second-acquisition cost; never split 50/50. Count ALL billable work: calibration in the physical ledger, ordinary measurement, discovery, failed discovery, proposal, rejected candidates, parent/candidate promotion runs, inheritance overhead, permitted retries, failed calls that incur cost, pre-abort spend.
break_even_rule: C_X(k) = cumulative all-in strategy cost when X earns its kth verified measurement result. Break-even = earliest common k where C_X(k) <= C_Y(k) AND X never returns above Y at any later common observed k. Fewer verified results: no break-even. Transient crossover is transient, not break-even.
budget_reservation_feasibility_note: Precontact static/config inspection of the repository's Hermes/provider invocation path (hermes -z <prompt> --usage-file <path>; no max output tokens passthrough; no bounded retry/API-call count in the controller; timeout alone does not bound billable tokens) establishes NO finite conservative R_i can be proven and enforced without building a new provider gateway, which the frozen contract forbids. The correct precontact result is NO_GO_BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT. This implementation encodes that gate rather than working around it.

calibration.feasibility: If calibration cannot complete under $5 or T > $8: NO_GO_CALIBRATION_FEASIBILITY. This branch builds and tests calibration machinery with deterministic fake fixtures only; no live paid calibration.
calibration.form: one raw-usage telemetry preflight plus one baseline maintenance task from each of 3 task families; namespace CAL; disposable worker state; calibration tasks never reused

causal_boundary: C versus B tests the incremental economic value of allowing continued method improvement after the common first fork. It does NOT independently establish that inheriting the first improvement caused better discovery of the second improvement. Permitted: 'The second improvement was discovered while operating under the inherited method.' Forbidden: 'The first improvement caused the second improvement to be discovered.'
completed_repetition: first common acquisition terminal accept/reject; C second acquisition terminal accept/reject; A/B/C each execute all 9 measurement tasks; all cost records reconcile; all method/evaluator/task hashes reconcile; no scientific abort. Candidate rejection, zero success, and negative economics are normal completed outcomes.

complexity_gate.note: No code golf, minification, generated runtime, or complexity moved into odd files to game the rule. Tests/fixtures/documentation make the system auditable. Runtime LOC reported honestly and separately from test/support LOC.
complexity_gate.on_violation: STOP PRECONTACT with NO_GO_IMPLEMENTATION_COMPLEXITY. Do not fix the preregistration afterward.
rules: maximum 2 COMPOUND-specific runtime executable Python modules
<=500 nonblank/noncomment lines of COMPOUND scientific runtime/controller code total

generation_plan.1: common first acquisition, exact B/C fork, fresh matched A/B/C measurement (3 tasks)
generation_plan.2: C receives one additional acquisition opportunity, fresh matched A/B/C measurement (3 tasks)
generation_plan.3: no new acquisition, fresh matched A/B/C measurement (3 tasks)

mutable_treatment: A small receiver-bounded research_method artifact. Airlock itself is NOT the treatment. The method may affect how allowed maintenance work is approached, how allowed receiver feedback is interpreted, and how a later method improvement is proposed. It may NOT modify or control: evaluator, protected tests, task generator, task schedule, cost meter, price table, spend rules, promotion criteria, model/provider config, hidden measurement work, reporting, controller. Every model contact begins with fresh worker/profile state; Nightshift persistent writable Hermes profile must not be used as lineage state. Only the exact receiver-authorized method artifact and explicitly allowed receiver feedback may cross generations.
nine_task_arithmetic: D1 = complete first-acquisition debt. B repays inside COMPOUND-001 only if D1 + C_B(9) <= C_A(9); with average per-task costs a, b: a - b >= D1 / 9. If D1 > C_A(9): rapid payback mathematically impossible inside this horizon (not longer-horizon falsification).

partitions.calibration: namespace CAL, 3 tasks (one per family), disposable worker state, never reused
partitions.discovery_per_acquisition: 3 fresh tasks (one per family); may inform the method proposal; never enter the production numerator
partitions.measurement: 3 fresh family-balanced tasks per generation, matched A/B/C instances within each repetition, never used in discovery or promotion
partitions.promotion_per_acquisition: 3 fresh promotion tasks, parent and candidate execute the exact same three; small selection gate only, labeled PROVISIONALLY_ACCEPTED_FOR_LINEAGE, not proof of general superiority
partitions.proposal_per_acquisition: exactly 1 paid proposal invocation, exactly 1 candidate, no replacement after rejection

phenomena: AMORTIZATION: one accepted process improvement incurs acquisition debt, then gets reused on later fresh work.

SUCCESSIVE_IMPROVEMENT: a lineage already containing one accepted process improvement later incurs another acquisition cost, and that later improvement creates incremental economic value on fresh work. Repeatedly reusing one trick is not compounding.
pooled_economics: For completed repetitions: POOL SUMS, never average per-repetition ratios. pooled_cost_X = sum of standalone strategy costs; pooled_verified_X = sum of verified measurement results; pooled_cost_per_verified_X = pooled_cost_X / pooled_verified_X (+infinity if zero). B pooled cost includes full D1 every repetition; C includes full D1 + D2 every repetition. A positive pooled X-over-Y comparison additionally requires pooled_verified_X >= pooled_verified_Y.

positive_claim_requirements.causal_boundary_restatement: This does not establish that the first inherited improvement caused better second-stage discovery.
positive_claim_requirements.one_time_amortization_only_if: B repays complete first acquisition debt vs A inside nine tasks AND B produces no less verified output.
positive_claim_requirements.permitted_positive_prose: Within the frozen task distribution, three-generation horizon, and budget, continued receiver-qualified method improvement produced lower acquisition-cost-adjusted cost per independently verified result than both an unchanged matched control and an exact one-improvement-frozen control.
successive_improvement_economic_advantag: C gets a second PROVISIONALLY_ACCEPTED_FOR_LINEAGE change while operating from common first-improvement state
second method actually used on untouched G2/G3 measurement
C repays D2 relative to B within six downstream measurement tasks
same C-over-B direction in at least 2/3 completed repetitions
pooled C output >= pooled B output
pooled C acquisition-adjusted $/verified result < pooled B
pooled C economics also finish better than A under same output-preservation rule

accept_only_if_all: candidate verifies at least 2/3 promotion tasks
candidate verifies no fewer than parent
candidate verified-results-per-metered-dollar strictly greater than parent on those promotion tasks
exact parent and candidate hashes bind to receipt
candidate remains inside frozen method-change bound
provisional_selection_rule.otherwise: REJECT with no replacement candidate; rejected candidate cost remains fully charged

question: Within a frozen small software-maintenance task distribution, a three-generation horizon, and a bounded direct-dollar budget, can independently accepted improvements to an AI research/work method lower the acquisition-cost-adjusted price of later independently verified work?
reservation_rule: Before EVERY paid invocation, compute a conservative maximum possible charge R_i from the frozen price table, an ENFORCED maximum billable resource envelope, all permitted billable token classes, maximum output, maximum context/input exposure, permitted retries, and any other billable quantity. Observed average price is NOT a reservation. Require settled_physical_spend + all_current_inflight_reservations + R_i <= 50.00, and during calibration also settled_calibration_spend + calibration_inflight_reservations + R_i <= 5.00. Post the reservation BEFORE contact; on settle, remove it and replace with independently reconstructed actual cost. If actual exceeds reservation: ABORT_BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT_FAILURE. If no finite conservative R_i can be proven and enforced: STOP PRECONTACT with NO_GO_BUDGET_ENFORCEMENT.
rsi_006_standing: unchanged: Q6_MECHANISM_HOLDS, NO_GO_Q6_QUALIFICATION_BINDING_COMPLEXITY, productivity experiment never authorized/run, no productivity advantage/disadvantage established, no Q7. COMPOUND-001 is a new study; it does not reopen RSI-006.
scope_note: Rapid-payback feasibility study. Failure to repay inside nine measurement tasks does not falsify 90-task payback, long-lived deployment economics, months-long amortization, other task distributions, other models, or indefinite recursive improvement. The task count must not be enlarged later to manufacture success.
six_task_arithmetic: D2 = C's second-acquisition debt, with six downstream measurement tasks (G2+G3). D2 + C_C(G2:G3) <= C_B(G2:G3); with averages b, c: b - c >= D2 / 6. If D2 > C_B(G2:G3): second acquisition cannot repay inside six tasks even if C's downstream execution became free. Do not increase the horizon to rescue this.
strategy_threshold_formula: T = round_up_to_$0.25(30 * c_max), where c_max is the maximum independently reconstructed cost among the 3 calibration maintenance-task calls; identical T for A/B/C
strategy_threshold_rule: Before a strategy-charged invocation: settled_strategy_cost + allocated acquisition debt + strategy_inflight_reservations + R_i <= T. For the shared first acquisition, future debt must remain admissible in BOTH standalone B and standalone C ledgers before another common acquisition invocation starts. If the next invocation cannot fit, do not start it; record STRATEGY_CONTACT_THRESHOLD_REACHED.

tracks.A: UNCHANGED: frozen baseline research method throughout.
tracks.B: ONE_IMPROVEMENT_FROZEN: shares the exact first acquisition with C; after the first acquisition reaches its receiver accept/reject outcome, B and C fork from the exact same state; B then freezes permanently.
tracks.C: SUCCESSIVE_IMPROVEMENT_LINEAGE: starts from the exact same first-fork state as B; in generation 2 only, C gets one additional bounded process-improvement acquisition opportunity.

unequal_output_rule: If V_X < V_Y: X cannot claim economic payback/superiority over Y. If V_X = V_Y: compare complete all-in cost. If V_X > V_Y: X may show advantage only if it reaches Y's final verified-output count at no greater cumulative all-in cost; extra output reported separately. No winning by failure or skipping.
unit_of_work: one fresh isolated task whose submitted patch satisfies the complete receiver-owned acceptance contract. Binary: 1 verified result or 0. No partial credit. Failures still cost money.
zero_success_rule: verified results = 0 implies verified-results-per-dollar = 0 and dollars-per-verified-result = +infinity. Never omit it. Both zero: no economic-superiority/payback claim. One zero, other >0: the zero-output strategy cannot win because it spent less.
